source: StreetSmart Form Review — Matt Croom's daily audit of every submitted form (full packet corpus)

latest.summary: 58 submissions reviewed for the Central calendar day of Saturday 10/17/2026: 26 air job / OWL forms, 15 Trailer Inspection Forms, 6 Trailer Readiness Forms, 6 H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Forms, and 5 Supervision Days job close-outs. Three further submissions arrived inside the 10/17 window but carry earlier

confirm.text: Follow-up: confirm whether the LEL sensor was replaced or repaired, and whether coverage of the shaker area was maintained while it was off. Flores filed a second daily for the same location at 10:20 PM and that form carries no note on the sensor either way, so its current status is not documented.
2. Bryan Medlin — trailer 601, CSRHI Andrews shop, 5:17 PM, Trailer Readiness Form. Equipment defect reported under "Is anything wrong or missing? If so what and who was notified?":
"Work pack was leaking air from the hose it's on the work bench"
Follow-up: confirm the workpack is out of service and tagged, and confirm who was notified — the form names the problem but not a notified party.
3. Brianda Sandoval — trailer 606, Unnamed Road, Midland, 4:45 PM, Trailer Inspection Form. A note against the Truck Ball Size Photo reads:
"2" didn't disconnect"

This appears to describe a 2-inch ball or coupler that would not release, which would be a towing-equipment issue, but the entry is three words and the form's "Comments or Concerns for Management" field was left as N/A. Needs Sandoval's confirmation of what it refers to before it is treated as a defect.
Stop work / unsafe conditions — needs confirmation, not action

These are selections on the "What did we observe?" multi-select, reported so the technician can confirm what was meant. They are not confirmed events. No form filed on 10/17 selected "Stop work authority utilized."

One form is not the routine mis-selection pattern and is worth treating as real: Baldemar Bracamontes, XTO, TXL 27 Unit 3 2773JH, 12:05 PM, job 35854, selected "Unsafe conditions" together with "Atmospheric hazards tested prior to first break" — and unlike the usual pattern his narrative names an actual condition: "Had meeting and made sure to take the time to point out the flooded location and how that could affect the job at hand. Tested bleeders prior to first break and job got completed safely." A flooded location is a specific, identified hazard that was discussed and worked around, so the selection looks deliberate rather than habitual. Worth confirming with him and noting for the location.
Seven forms selected "Stop work authority was discussed" — the routine pre-job item, not a stop-work event:

Two forms do record a "No" to "Did we leave the location better than we found it?" — Nathan Contreras (job 35917) and Dawson Drake (job 35963_1) — but both explain it in the narrative ("Job reassigned" and "There was no trash on location to be picked up"), so neither reads as a safety item.

Missing required documentation
Air jobs

SM Energy, Litterbox CTB, NORM air job, ticket 102118E, AT# 175. Board assigns Stefanie Kirschke and Robbie Henigan 1099. No air job submission was received from either technician. Kirschke was on the job — she filed a Trailer Inspection Form for trailer 175 at Williams Rd, Big Lake at 10:40 AM. The same ticket 102118E also appears on the 10/16 board, so this is a running multi-day NORM job and the technicians may have paused it in StreetSmart rather than ending it, which would produce no email. Needs confirmation before it is treated as a missing submission.

All other air jobs are fully covered — one submission per named technician on Nunn 14 1 SWD-TK551, Zant Hurt Blalock E Unit 1 0116AH (both crews), Elkin 21O 15H, Elkin 21Y 25H, Alleder Welch 33G 207H, Mary 18 1HB, Zoey 4-16C 103H, TXL 27 Unit 3 2773JH, Watkins-Burkitt 1204G 10H, Shackelford 40-12D 4H and Preston-Freeman 15A 101H. clean.text: Nothing requiring attention from: Nathan Contreras (three Trailer Inspection Forms for trailer 600 and the Trailer Readiness Form for 600, plus air job 35917 — full trailer coverage single-handed); Luis Zarate (two Trailer Inspection Forms for trailer 607 and three air jobs, 35920, 35922 and 35969_1, all with complete close-outs and detailed narratives); Dawson Drake (air job 35963_1, Nunn 14 1, complete); Jeremy Norris (Trailer Inspection Form and Trailer Readiness Form for trailer 603, and air job 35874 — only the one unanswered housekeeping question); Cindy Smith (air job 35875, Mary 18 1HB, with the fullest atmospheric-testing narrative of the day); Justin Pack (H2S daily for FESCO Lilly #1, complete cascade and hydro entries, only the one stale Loud Alarm photo); Ralph Forbes (H2S daily for BPX State Blake, the most detailed cascade and hydro record in the set); Jacob Hernandez (air

Trailer forms of both kinds, and the equipment sections of the H2S daily, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review — I can read the capture timestamp and the field label, but not the image. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside those images, not as text, so none of them were verified today. Separately, this review ran at 11:00 PM Central; submissions that land after midnight with a 10/17 form date would not have been captured and would need picking up tomorrow.

61 of 61 submissions read. The job board was available: Blake Walton's 10/17/2026 email arrived at 10:00 AM Central with both workbooks, and the "10-17 DRAFT" sheet of the ArkLaTex board and the "10-17" sheet of the Permian Basin board were used. 61 manned board rows were checked for coverage — 16 ETX and 45 WTX — of which 39 are active assignments and the remainder are standby, days off, WTX support or unassigned.
